verdict: Mastercard's net revenue rose 14% to $9.3B as card spending grew around the world, and net income rose 19% to $4.4B — another quarter of the toll-booth model doing its work.

segments.name: Payment network
segments.note: Fees every time a Mastercard is swiped, tapped or used online — gross dollar volume was $2.9 trillion in the quarter, up 8% in local currency.

segments.name: Value-added services and solutions
segments.note: Fraud protection, data analytics, consulting and identity services sold on top of the network — growing twice as fast as the network itself.

flow.grossPlain: Mastercard reports revenue already net of the $5,997M of rebates and incentives it pays banks and merchants to win card business — so there is no separate cost-of-revenue line in its books. The costs were taken out before revenue was counted.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Salaries, technology and offices for the people who run the network — by far Mastercard's biggest cost.

opex.name: Advertising and marketing
opex.note: Brand campaigns, sponsorships and the 'Priceless' advertising.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, data centers, equipment and acquired technology.

opex.name: Provision for litigation
opex.note: Legal provisions, including ATM surcharge complaints and merchants who opted out of the U.S. merchant class litigation — Mastercard flags this as a special item.

takeaways.title: Spending held up everywhere
takeaways.text: Gross dollar volume rose 8% in local currency, cross-border volume rose 12% and switched transactions rose 9% — the growth was broad, not one market carrying the rest.

takeaways.title: Services are the growth engine
takeaways.text: Value-added services net revenue grew 20% to $3.8B — fraud, data and consulting products now bring in over 40% of Mastercard's revenue.

takeaways.title: Six dollars in ten became operating profit
takeaways.text: The operating margin was 60.2%, up from 58.7% a year ago. Net income rose 19% to $4.4B despite an $82M litigation provision flagged as a special item.

oneTimers: An $82M litigation provision — covering ATM non-discrimination surcharge complaints, a change in estimate on claims from merchants who opted out of the U.S. merchant class litigation, and other legal matters — is flagged by Mastercard as a special item. Excluding it and a $2M loss on equity investments, adjusted net income was $4.5B and adjusted EPS was $5.04.
otherDetail: Other income (expense) was −$101M: $88M of investment income and $31M of other income, outweighed by $218M of interest expense and a $2M loss on equity investments.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference. The first row is net revenue (already net of rebates), so there is no cost-of-revenue row.
